experiments.name: Venue search on Railway (Meilisearch) with Xano ep119 fallback - assistant + Discovery, 50% of users
experiments.goal: Faster search without reliability loss
experiments.primary_metric: assistant search_ms + total latency (table 79 search_engine), Discovery ep119 duration split by X-Search-Engine header; fallback + error rate
experiments.guardrail: fallback rate <5%, error rate not above ep119
experiments.dates_note: Assistant live 2026-10-26 01:08 UTC at 15%; Discovery (ep119 proxy) live 01:39 UTC at 15%; both ramped to 20% at 01:53 UTC (owner request, before the 25% ramp rule had data). Owner account forced on. Hourly data sync from 01:10 UTC; 2026-10-26 22:03 UTC search-api circuit breaker (503 for 120 s after a Meili timeout) + Meili query timeout 1.5 s; 22:04 ep119 Railway wait 3 s -> 2 s; ~22:20 ramp 20% -> 50% (ep119 $rw_pct + REC_RAILWAY_SEARCH_PCT, owner); 23:32 root-cause fix: search-api/sync no longer PATCH /experimental-features on every reload (Meili held it 5-48 s).
experiments.design: A/B by stable user bucket sha256('railsearch:'+user_id)%100 (20% railway / 80% ep119); same bucket in the assistant (REC_RAILWAY_SEARCH_PCT) and Discovery (ep119 $rw_pct), so users who were in at 15% stay in

results.note: baseline: 2026-10-25 end-to-end from outside Railway, real search shapes: ep119 cache-miss p50 1653 / p90 3000 ms; ep119 hit 268 ms; Railway 158 / 186 ms (+~230 ms first search per user for auth/me)

Launch check: Georgia barn search on Railway took 234 ms (assistant ep119 avg ~4.1s); whole answer 12.6s. Parity 22/23 same venue sets; popular-sort order drift from stale click counts (now synced hourly).

Discovery launch: owner 0.76/1.03s, in-bucket test account 0.98/2.28s on Railway vs 2.5-5.1s ep119; forced fallback (SEARCH_ENABLED=0) returned full results. First push 01:33 failed ('Invalid op: in'), auto-rolled back in 15s, 2 real searches failed. Ramp 15->20% at 01:53 UTC (owner).

A/B readout 01:53-21:00 UTC: Discovery cache-miss median 0.44 s Railway vs 1.52 s ep119 (p90 1.40 vs 6.55 s), IP-cluster 95% CI on the difference -1.85..-0.64 s, Mann-Whitney p 7e-11; cache hits identical (~55% of requests). Planner search step 68 ms vs 3,997 ms (7 vs 45 requests, p~1e-5 per user); whole answer 9.4 s vs 14.4 s (loose, CI -8.2..-1.0 s). Fallback 9% (31/345, all http_0), 24 of 31 at 16:00 and 19:00 UTC: ramp rule NOT met before the fixes.

Root cause of the fallbacks: Meilisearch freezes (8-65 s, ~11/day) - not memory/CPU, not the hourly sync itself; search-api's sync-meta check also blocked user searches on a 60 s client. Fixed 22:03 (breaker + fail-fast meta read). 3 of 4 breaker trips 22:50-23:25 sat inside a PATCH /experimental-features (5.4-48 s) -> fixed 23:32. One more 48 s freeze at 23:58 with no PATCH: residual cause unknown.

50% read 22:51-23:25 UTC: 179 Discovery searches, all 200; Railway misses median 0.49 s vs ep119 1.57 s; breaker caught 17 searches (fast http_503 fallbacks); slow http_0 5/79 (3 of them instant Xano-side connect failures). Next: 1 clean day with the 23:32 fix -> 100%.

experiments.decision: Ramp to 25% when the brief says green (>=50 Railway requests, fallback <5%, search p50 >=30% faster)
confounds_noted: Railway answers enter the shared ep119 24 h cache (cache key excludes auth), so cache hits can't be attributed to an arm
Owner account forced to Railway (Discovery logs have no user id)
risks: data freshness: hourly sync (was daily 08:30 UTC)
auth still depends on Xano auth/me
